content.value_statement: Genomic interval machine learning requires careful preprocessing, embedding training, and validation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical geniml workflows for BED files and single-cell chromatin data.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Region2Vec, BEDspace, scEmbed, consensus peaks, and geniml utilities.
Provides installation guidance for geniml core and optional machine learning dependencies.
Outlines BED file tokenization, universe building, model training, and evaluation workflows.
Shows command-line examples for region embeddings, BEDspace preprocessing, universe building, and BEDshift randomization.
Describes evaluation metrics and quality checks for embeddings, tokenization coverage, and universes.
Connects geniml workflows with scanpy, BEDbase, Hugging Face, R reticulate, and StarSpace.
limitations: It does not run analyses unless the user has geniml and required dependencies installed.
It depends on correct genome assemblies, BED formats, metadata files, and universe references supplied by the user.
Large scATAC-seq or universe-building workflows may need substantial memory and compute resources.
It provides workflow guidance, not biological interpretation or publication-ready statistical review.

use_cases.title: Train region embeddings for bulk assays
use_cases.description: Prepare BED files, tokenize against a universe, train Region2Vec, and evaluate embedding quality.

use_cases.title: Cluster single-cell chromatin profiles
use_cases.description: Use scEmbed with AnnData and scanpy to create cell embeddings for clustering and visualization.

use_cases.title: Build a consensus peak universe
use_cases.description: Choose CC, CCF, ML, or HMM methods and evaluate the resulting reference peak set.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a geniml workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: I have BED files from {assay_type} experiments and want to compare genomic regions. Recommend the right geniml workflow and explain the required inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Region2Vec training
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Region2Vec plan for {number_of_bed_files} BED files using {genome_assembly}. Include tokenization, universe requirements, training parameters, and evaluation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a scEmbed analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me use scEmbed on an AnnData file named {adata_file}. Include tokenization, model training, embedding export, scanpy clustering, and quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare universe-building methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare CC, CCF, ML, and HMM universe-building methods for {assay_type} data with {sample_count} samples. Recommend parameters and validation metrics.

output_examples.input: I have ATAC-seq BED files and need region embeddings.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step Region2Vec workflow with universe preparation, tokenization thresholds, training settings, and evaluation metrics.

output_examples.input: I need to cluster scATAC-seq cells with geniml.
output_examples.output: A scEmbed analysis plan that covers AnnData preparation, cell tokenization, embedding generation, scanpy integration, and clustering validation.

output_examples.input: Which consensus peak method should I use for noisy ChIP-seq peaks?
output_examples.output: A method comparison that recommends CCF or ML, explains boundary uncertainty, and lists universe quality checks.

best_practices: Verify genome assembly consistency before tokenization, universe building, or model evaluation.
Track parameters, random seeds, input files, and universe versions for reproducible genomic ML results.
Evaluate outputs with multiple metrics, visualizations, and biological sanity checks before downstream use.
anti_patterns: Do not train embeddings before checking tokenization coverage and universe quality.
Do not mix genome assemblies or incompatible BED coordinate conventions in one workflow.
Do not treat clustering or search results as biological conclusions without external validation.

faq.question: What data does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on genomic interval data, especially BED files, chromatin accessibility data, and single-cell ATAC-seq workflows.

faq.question: When should I use Region2Vec?
faq.answer: Use Region2Vec when you need unsupervised embeddings for genomic regions or region sets without rich metadata labels.

faq.question: When should I use BEDspace?
faq.answer: Use BEDspace when metadata labels are important and you need joint embeddings for regions and labels.

faq.question: Does this skill install geniml automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation commands and workflow guidance, but the user controls all installation and execution steps.

faq.question: Can it analyze single-cell ATAC-seq data?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes scEmbed workflows that integrate with AnnData and scanpy for embeddings, clustering, and visualization.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Prepare valid BED files, matching genome assembly information, metadata files when needed, and a suitable universe or plan to build one.
